title: Vocabulary registry
description: A vocabulary is a closed set of named alternatives for one configuration choice: where the wing sits, which way the propellers face, what keeps a flying boat upright at rest. A value is a definition, not a quantity. What makes the layer more than a glossary is `admits`: the parameters that exist only when a value is chosen.

id.description: Stable slug, unique across the WHOLE corpus: constraints, parameters, units' local names aside, and vocabularies share one namespace.

applies_to.description: The kind of thing the choice is made about: wing, propulsion, hull. A slug, not yet a registry; it says where a consumer hangs the choice.

definition.description: What is being chosen, independent of any tool.

values.description: The alternatives. At least two: a choice of one is not a choice.

exhaustive.description: True only when the source says these are all the alternatives. False is the honest default: a design outside the list is not thereby wrong, and a consumer reports it and does not reject it.

id.description: Unique within its vocabulary. A consumer writes it verbatim.

admits.description: Parameter ids that exist ONLY under values that admit them. A parameter named by any value of a vocabulary may be held only when the chosen value names it; a parameter no value names is not this vocabulary's business.
